core_obligations: Reduce to the strictly henselian case (proof lines 19425-19431): the construction of h, i and beta depends only on the base change of X and K to Spec(O^sh_{S,s}), so one may assume S strictly henselian with closed point s; local acyclicity is preserved by this base change.

Compute the stalk (proof lines 19433-19445): for a geometric point x of X_s, equivalently a geometric point mapping to s, the stalk of i^{-1}beta at x equals the stalk of beta at x by the stalk-pullback lemma, and since S is strictly henselian the morphism h : X_t -> X satisfies X_t x_X Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) = F_{x,t}.

Identify with alpha (proof lines 19446-19457): hence the stalk (beta)_{x} is the map K_x -> Rh_*(K|_{X_t})_x = R Gamma(F_{x,t}, K), which is exactly the map alpha_{K,x,t} appearing in the definition of local acyclicity.

Conclude (proof lines 19458-19462): since a map of etale sheaves is an isomorphism if and only if it is an isomorphism on stalks, the identification of the stalk map with alpha proves that i^{-1}beta is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Base change to the strict henselisation of S at s and use that local acyclicity is preserved.
Compute the stalk of i^{-1}beta using the stalk-pullback lemma and the description of the Milnor fibre in the strictly henselian case.
Recognise the resulting map as alpha and apply the stalk criterion for isomorphisms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the comparison map beta, after pulling back along i, with the stalk-level map alpha of the definition of local acyclicity (statement lines 19419-19422). The proof (proof lines 19424-19462) reduces to a strictly henselian base, computes the stalk of i^{-1}beta at a geometric point using the stalk-pullback lemma and the identification of the Milnor fibre with the strict henselisation of X at the point, and concludes with the stalk criterion for isomorphisms. H2: one base change reduction and one stalk computation, both written out.
